verses.zh: （一篇诗。）你们要向耶和华唱新歌！因为他行过奇妙的事；他的右手和圣臂施行救恩。
verses.en: A psalm.Sing to the Lord a new song,[NOTE:1] for he performs[NOTE:2] amazing deeds.His right hand and his mighty armaccomplish deliverance.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 98. The psalmist summons the whole earth to praise God because he reveals his justice and delivers Israel.
A new song is appropriate because the Lord is constantly intervening in the world as its just king. See Ps 96:1.

The perfect verbal forms in vv. 1-3 are understood here as describing characteristic divine activities. Another option is to translate them as present perfects, “has performed…has accomplished deliverance, etc.” referring to completed actions that have continuing results.
verses.commentary:
98:1 "O sing to the Lord a new song" This is a Qal
IMPERATIVE. One can see why Psalm 95; 96; and 98 were placed close together
(i.e., Book 4, Psalm 90-106) in the Psalter by the editor(s).

The "new song" was a response from the covenant people to their God's deliverance,
forgiveness, and displays of power (cf. Ps. 98:1b, 33:3; 40:3; 96:1; 144:9; 149:1; Isa. 42:10;
Rev. 5:9; 14:3). YHWH acted on their behalf. He, and He alone, was responsible (Ps. 98:1c). However,
Ps. 37:40 shows that YHWH's salvation/deliverance is linked to human faith and faithfulness. The covenant
(see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT)
combines YHWH's sovereign initiation and mankind's expected obedient, continuing response.

▣ "His right hand" Theologically this is parallel to Isa. 52:10. The victory is His and His alone!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "have gained victory" This VERB (BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil
PERFECT) means "to save," "to bring victory" (cf. Isa. 59:16; 63:5). The victory
(depending on the contextual intended timeframe) could refer to

- initial creation (i.e., victory over watery chaos, i.e., Ps. 65:7; 89:9-10; 93:3-4)

- the exodus/conquest (cf. Isa. 51:9-10, i.e., Red Sea and Jordan River)

- vanquishing the gods (elohim) of the nations (cf. Ps. 2:1; 65:7-8)

- return from exile (cf. Isaiah 40-45)

- ultimate victory over evil (i.e., Gen. 3:15; Matt. 1:21; Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21)

verses.en: The Lord demonstrates his power to deliver;[NOTE:1] in the sight of the nations he reveals his justice.
notes: Heb “his right hand delivers for him and his holy arm.” The right hand and arm symbolize his power as a warrior-king (see Isa 52:10). His arm is “holy” in the sense that it is in a category of its own; God’s power is incomparable.

106:45).

▣ "All the ends of the earth" See Contextual Insights, A.

The NIDOTTE, p. 521, has a list of how the phrase, "the ends of the earth," is used.

- YHWH's name and praise ‒ Ps. 48:10; Isa. 42:10

- fear of God ‒ Ps. 67:7

- knowledge of God's rule ‒ Ps. 59:13

- the salvation of God ‒ Ps. 98:3; Isa. 49:6; 52:10

- His message of redemption ‒ Isa. 48:20; 62:11

- Messianic King's reign ‒ Ps. 2:7; Micah 5:4

For me, this international, multi-ethnic, universal emphasis is the focus and
fruition of "monotheism" (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM).

The AB (pp. 365-366) revocalizes the two PREFECT VERBS to make them
IMPERATIVES.

- "remember" ‒ BDB 269, KB 269 (this would refer to Israel)

- "see" ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157 (this would refer to "all the ends of the earth")

Although this makes sense, it does not fit the string of PERFECTS and
the parallel between Ps. 98:2 and 3. The IMPERATIVES would fit better with the next
strophe (Ps. 98:4-6).

verses.en: Let the sea and everything in it shout,along with the world and those who live in it.
verses.commentary:
98:7-9 The last strophe has three JUSSIVES expressing the need for personified
creation (cf. Ps. 104:19-22) as well as humans to praise the righteous Judge of creation.

- let the seas roar ‒ BDB 947, KB 1266, Qal IMPERFECT used in a

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

- let the rivers clap ‒ BDB 561, KB 567, Qal IMPERATIVE used in a

Numbers 1 and 2 are parallel and denote humans. Numbers 3 and 4 are parallel and denote

verses.zh: 因为他来要审判遍地。他要按公义审判世界，按公正审判万民。
verses.en: before the Lord.For he comes to judge the earth.He judges the world fairly,[NOTE:1] and the nations in a just manner.
notes: Heb “the deliverance of our God,” with “God” being a subjective genitive (= God delivers).
verses.commentary:
98:9 "He is coming" This is a Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE. When thinking of
YHWH "coming," several items must be emphasized.

- He has never left. He is always here!

- His special coming or presence can be for

- blessings

- judgment (as here, cf. Ps. 9:7-8; 96:13)

- His coming brings the expectation of a new day (i.e., the restoration of the fellowship of Eden)

- This theological concept has been supplemented by the two comings of the Messiah.

- the first fulfilled most OT predictions

- the second will consummate YHWH's reign

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is the content of the "new song"?

- What victory is Ps. 98:1 addressing?

- How does Ps. 98:3 relate to Genesis 12?

- What regular event in Israel's cultic calendar does Ps. 98:4-6 relate to?

- Explain the different ways YHWH's coming can be understood.

- "in the sight of the nations," Ps. 98:2

- "all the ends of the earth have seen," Ps. 98:3

Please read SPECIAL TOPIC:
YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN. It is the integrating center of my theology!

- YHWH is coming as King (see full note at Ps. 97:1) and Judge to the whole world and especially to Israel. He is coming as
the One who made promises to the Patriarchs (cf. Ps. 98:3a).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

- The first strophe has six PERFECTS (completed action) which detail what YHWH
has done (or will do; the time element in Hebrew VERBS is determined by context).

- has done wonderful things, Ps. 98:1

- has gained victory, Ps. 98:1

- has made known His salvation, Ps. 98:2

- has revealed His righteousness, Ps. 98:2

- has remembered His lovingkindness and faithfulness, Ps. 98:3

- all the earth has seen His salvation, Ps. 98:3
